originalTitle: US stocks today: Nasdaq lags on angst over AI spending ahead of earnings reports
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the US stock market: the Nasdaq (a group of technology stocks) went down because investors are worried that companies are spending too much on artificial intelligence (AI). On the other hand, the Dow (another group of stocks) went up, and the S&P 500 (a broader group of stocks) stayed about the same. This happened because oil prices are lower, which is good for the market, but there are also concerns about international tensions and trade issues. These mixed results are happening just before some big technology companies are set to release their earnings reports, which can affect how investors feel about the market. Overall, investors are being cautious about what might happen next.

originalTitle: American Express Q2 profit rises driven by higher spending and fewer delinquencies
simplifiedContent: American Express made more money in the second quarter of the year, with an 8% increase in profit. This happened because people used their American Express cards more and were better at paying their bills on time, which means fewer late payments. The company also got more new customers to sign up for its high-end services, which shows that its marketing efforts are working. However, American Express did spend 12% more on things like advertising and improving its products, which is a lot. This increase in spending is likely an investment in the company's future growth.

originalTitle: ACC Q1 Results: Profit plunges 60% to Rs 147 crore on lower sales
simplifiedContent: ACC Ltd, a company owned by the Adani Group, recently released its financial results for the first quarter of the year. Unfortunately, the company's profit decreased by 60.8% to Rs 147 crore, which is a significant drop. This happened because the company sold fewer products, leading to a 7.75% decrease in revenue compared to the same time last year. The company's higher costs also affected its earnings, but it did see some positive signs with its premium products gaining market share. This decline in profit matters because it can affect the company's overall performance and potentially impact its stock price.

originalTitle: Yields ease, but Iran war keeps rate-hike bets alive
simplifiedContent:
Here is a rewritten version of the news item in simple language: 
The yields on US government bonds, which are like loans to the government, recently went down a bit. However, because of the conflict with Iran, some people still think that interest rates might go up soon. This is important because when interest rates go up, it can affect the stock market and the economy. The yields on government bonds are being watched closely to see what might happen with interest rates. The situation with Iran is making it hard to predict what will happen next with interest rates.

originalTitle: Yen records biggest weekly drop in over two months, dollar climbs for the week
simplifiedContent: The value of the Japanese yen has dropped the most it has in over two months. At the same time, the value of the US dollar has increased over the past week. This means that if you exchanged yen for dollars, you would get fewer dollars than you would have a week ago. This is important because it can affect the price of imports and exports between countries, as well as investments in foreign markets. The change in currency values can impact the overall economy and may be of interest to investors who have money in international markets.

originalTitle: Stocks edge back up as oil prices pause climb but yields hover near highs
simplifiedContent: The stock market is going back up a little bit after a pause. This is happening because oil prices have stopped increasing for now. At the same time, interest rates, also known as yields, are staying near their highest points. This matters because when oil prices are high and interest rates are high, it can be a challenge for the stock market to go up. The stock market going back up is a positive sign, despite these challenges.
